narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 82.1% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. In practical terms, you were judged much more likely than not to struggle at the bar, and that risk signal was decisive.

The strongest factor was your third-year class rank: you were in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year rank was the second most influential factor; also at the lowest decile versus an accepted average near the sixth, it reinforced the same concern. Your LSAT score was the third most important factor. At 35 it was below the accepted average of about 37, but its influence pointed toward passing, so it was a relative point in your favor rather than the reason for denial.

You should ask admissions for feedback and whether any holistic review is possible, explaining context behind your class rank. Consider retaking the LSAT and building clear evidence of bar readiness through academic support, structured study plans, or relevant coursework. If this denial is final, ask what improved credentials and explanations a future application should include.
